(5) Real-Time HIL Integration Requirements Synchronizing signal flows, control behavior, and real-time simulation constraints required detailed preparation and iterative refinement. 8.6 Lessons Learned (1) Early Integration Across EMT, HIL, and Commissioning Workflows Is Critical Coordinating these activities from the outset reduces rework and improves the quality of control-tuning and validation. (2) Plant-Level Coordination Is Central to GFM Success GFM operation cannot be validated or deployed effectively without integrating plant- level supervisory functions early in the process. (3) Measurement Strategy Must Be Defined Before Field Activities Begin Early planning of measurement locations, sampling rates, and data interfaces ensures meaningful comparison between simulations and future field data. As a result: • Commissioning activities did not occur. • Field demonstration activities did not begin. • System-level validation tasks remained incomplete. • BP2 work was not initiated. These outcomes reflect a shortened period of performance - not technical deficiencies. 8.8 Overall Conclusions Budget Period 1 substantially advanced the modeling, validation, engineering readiness, and measurement infrastructure required for future grid-forming demonstrations at the Wheatridge hybrid facility. The work completed provides durable technical value for national efforts aimed at improving grid reliability under increasing inverter-based resource penetration. Despite the early end of BP1, the deliverables, EMT modeling frameworks, early positive-sequence structures, HIL capability, test plans, performance metrics, and site-measurement infrastructure, form a strong foundation for future research, demonstration, and potential commercial adoption of grid-forming inverter technologies. 9. Path Forward: The analytical, modeling, and preparatory engineering completed in this project has created a technically sound foundation for future evaluation and demonstration of grid-forming (GFM) inverter capabilities within a large hybrid renewable plant. Although field commissioning did not begin during BP1 due to early award termination, the modeling frameworks, HIL testbed, performance metric definitions, and plant-level measurement systems collectively establish a clear and executable path for subsequent demonstration and research. This chapter outlines the recommended next steps across commissioning, modeling, validation, data analysis, and broader industry engagement. 9.1 Future Demonstration Opportunities Complete Commissioning of GFM Resources Page 26 of 36 Award Number: DE-EE0010651 Recipient Name: Portland General Electric The commissioning procedures, mode-transition logic, and coordination requirements developed during BP1 can directly support future activation of GFM functions.
